newsitem.title: USA: House Bank Chair Leach opposes bank/commerce mix.
newsitem.headline: House Bank Chair Leach opposes bank/commerce mix.

text.p: House Banking Committee Chairman Jim Leach said on Wednesday he remains wary of financial modernization proposals that would allow unlimited combination of banks and commercial firms.
While he supports allowing banks to combine with securities underwriters and insurance firms, the Iowa Republican said proposals that go further "should be looked upon with great wariness."
Leach was testifying before the Banking Committee's Subcommittee on Capital Markets, Securities and Government-Sponsored Enterprises.
Leach has introduced a bill that would allow minimal mixing of banking and commerce.
Rep. Richard Baker, chairman of the capital markets subcommittee, has offered a bill that would impose virtually no limit on such combinations.
Leach said the general public would not favor unlimited combinations.
"Questions demand answering," Leach said. "Does the public have a vested interest in government-incentivized conglomeration or greater market competition?"
